newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey's Tupras buys 300,000 T crude.
newsitem.headline: Turkey's Tupras buys 300,000 T crude.

text.p: Turkey's state oil refiner Tupras confirmed on Wednesday it had bought 300,000 tonnes of Iranian, Syrian and Kazakh crude oil in a recent tender.
"We have decided to announce the purchase of 300,000 tonnes," a Tupras oficial told Reuters.
The official said Marc Rich took the bulk of the tender, selling 110,000 tonnes of Iranian heavy and 80,000 tonnes of Syrian light.
Tupras also accepted offers of 55,000 tonnes of Iranian heavy from BP and between 40-55,000 tonnes of Tengiz from Chevron. The tender, which closed on Friday, was for delivery on July 15-25.

The official declined to mention prices but traders said on Tuesday the Iranian heavy was heard priced at $1.50 below Dated Brent while the Syrian was believed accepted at 20 cents a barrel over the official selling price. No number were reported for the Tengiz barrels.
A delay in the resumption of Iraqi crude exports under the U.N. oil-for-food deal has raised the price of sour crudes and left many Mediterranean refiners, including Tupras, pinched.
